inputs_and_claim_classes.macvdmtool_facts: Inherited from root's reports/sprint-008/controller-recovery-source-review.json (source at M5 commit b22ae51e, not independently re-read here because it is only on the M5).
inputs_and_claim_classes.target_preflight: User/root relayed, not observed here: kernel.panic=10, systemd RuntimeWatchdogUSec=30s, RebootWatchdogUSec=2min, kernel 7.2.11-6-1-ARCH.
inputs_and_claim_classes.prior_live_evidence: Root reports: serial-mode VDM rc 0 (serial-mode-command.json), bidirectional serial shell (serial-bidirectional.json), orderly SSH reboot and return in about 34 s (orderly-reboot-001.json).
inputs_and_claim_classes.local_source_fact: Pinned m1n1 calls wdt_disable() during startup (sources/m1n1-baseline/src/main.c:245,285; src/wdt.c:14).
inputs_and_claim_classes.linux_systemd_semantics: General upstream Linux/systemd behavior (SysRq s/u/c, kernel.panic, runtime/reboot watchdog). Not verified against the target kernel or systemd build; each stage verifies the effect on the target.

key_findings.finding: macvdmtool is a reset/mode tool, not a recovery oracle. reboot sends one VDM and returns; exit 0 means the local ACE/VDM calls succeeded, not that the target reset or booted. There is no OS detection, liveness check, boot selection, power control or retry.

The tool sends nothing unless the M5's local AppleHPM register 0x3f bit 0 shows a connection. Whether a hard-hung target keeps that bit set is unknown, so hang-state resets must be proven, not assumed.

nop is not read-only: every recognized command unlocks the local ACE and enters/exits DBMa. The DBMa exit runs only in the destructor (no signal handler), so a killed macvdmtool may leave the M5 port controller in DBMa. Bound it with a timeout, but record a forced kill as 'ACE state unknown' rather than killing silently.

reboot serial = reboot VDM, wait about 1 s plus up to 3 s for the connected bit, then serial mode. A nonzero return after the reboot VDM was sent (e.g. 'Timed out') means the reset request was sent but serial re-enable failed, not that the reset failed. Use reboot serial so boot output is captured, and classify by stage of failure.

Healthy-Linux-first ordering is correct. While Linux runs and pets the watchdog, neither the 30 s runtime watchdog nor kernel.panic=10 can fire, so a reset at the VDM moment is attributable to the VDM. The watchdog stays a safety net for the orderly fallback.

Watchdog and panic settings make a naive hang test unprovable: panic=10 reboots 10 s after a panic, the 30 s runtime watchdog resets a dead kernel, and the 2 min reboot watchdog stays armed through a halt. Any hang test needs runtime-only panic=0, the watchdog verifiably inactive, and a hold window longer than every watchdog timeout before the VDM is sent.

The hardware watchdog does not cover the target use case: m1n1 disables it at startup, so a hung m1n1/HV/XNU experiment has no watchdog recovery. The VDM reset is the only independent path for those runs, which is why it must be qualified from a genuinely hung state.

An abrupt SoC reset with writable block filesystems risks journal replay or a dirty-bit EFI. SysRq s then u, waiting for completion and verifying root, /boot and the EFI system partition are read-only (or unmounted), reduces that to an expected clean-RO reset.

stages.actions: No resets. Record M1 boot_id, uname -r, /proc/cmdline hash, findmnt (all block filesystems, automount units for /boot or /efi), swapon, watchdog sysfs (state, timeout, nowayout if present), kernel.panic*, the SSH host key, macvdmtool binary SHA-256 against the build record, and a running M5 serial reader logging to a private file. Confirm the M1 Linux root is not the user's filesystem under repair and that the boot default and recovery copies are unchanged, with no pending one-shot boot override.
stages.gate: Any identity, hash, ownership or filesystem-under-repair doubt stops the qualification.

stages.actions: sync; SysRq s; SysRq u; wait for the kernel's emergency sync and remount completion messages; verify root, /boot and EFI are ro or not mounted, and avoid touching automount paths. Leave the watchdog and panic settings unchanged (safety net). Then M5: sudo macvdmtool reboot serial with a bounded timeout.
acceptance: Pre-reset verification shows every block-backed filesystem read-only (tmpfs may stay rw).
macvdmtool reached the reboot VDM; rc and stdout are recorded and classified per R4.
The serial log (M5 timestamps) shows boot output beginning only after the VDM time, with no orderly 'reboot:' shutdown message before it.
SSH returns with the pinned host key, a new boot_id, the same kernel and /proc/cmdline as baseline, within a budget well above the 34 s orderly figure (e.g. 180 s).
The current boot's kernel log shows no filesystem recovery, replay, corruption or error messages and no EFI dirty-bit warning; filesystems are rw again.
Repeated independently at least 3 times with identical outcomes.
stages.abort_and_fallback: If any filesystem is still rw after u, do not send the VDM; run an orderly systemctl reboot. If macvdmtool fails before the reboot VDM (no connection, no reply, VDM failed), boot_id is unchanged and SSH works: perform the orderly reboot to restore rw. If SSH does not return within budget, stop and require operator recovery; record the 2 min reboot watchdog as possibly active.

stages.precondition: S1 passed at least 3 times. A human-reachable physical recovery is available for the first runs, because a failed VDM leaves a halted target without SSH.
stages.actions: Runtime-only, reverting at reboot, no boot configuration edits: kernel.panic=0, the systemd runtime and reboot watchdog set to off, then verify every /sys/class/watchdog device is inactive, nowayout is 0 where exposed, and no process holds /dev/watchdog*. Preferred hang: systemctl halt (orderly unmount, CPUs stopped with interrupts off, power on). Optional later: SysRq s and u, verify RO, then SysRq c with panic=0.
acceptance: The serial log shows the halt or panic message, then silence; SSH is unreachable.
A hold window longer than every watchdog timeout (at least 3 min, above the 2 min reboot watchdog) passes with no reset or boot output. This is the discriminator proving no autonomous reset.
Only then sudo macvdmtool reboot serial; boot output starts after the VDM time; SSH returns with a new boot_id, the same kernel and cmdline, and a clean filesystem log.
Repeated at least 3 times before declaring unattended hang recovery.
stages.confounder_rule: If any watchdog cannot be shown inactive (nowayout=1, unknown driver, or the state attribute missing), or the target resets during the hold window, label the result WDT_CONFOUNDED_NOT_VDM_PROOF.
stages.panic_test_assessment: SysRq c with panic=0 adds an unclean crashed-kernel state but little reset-path information beyond halt (both stop CPUs with interrupts off). Run it only after halt-based S2 passes, only with verified RO block filesystems, and with the same watchdog-off proof and hold window.

stages.actions: Later: an m1n1-hosted parked experiment (the watchdog is disabled by m1n1), then VDM reboot serial and return to the preserved Linux default.
stages.note: m1n1's exception-proxy disconnect path can reboot the target by itself (src/uartproxy.c:285-291, src/hv/hv_exc.c:69-88). Record whether the host stream closed before the VDM so an autonomous reboot is not mistaken for a VDM reset.

addendum_halt_based_external_reset.relayed_preflight: CONFIG_WATCHDOG_NOWAYOUT unset, CONFIG_WATCHDOG_SYSFS unset, APPLE_WATCHDOG=y. SysRq s/u completed with /boot and EFI read-only but the Btrfs root still rw; explicit remount ro returned busy. Root correctly aborted the external reset under the S1 abort rule. No panic test was run.
why_sound: An orderly systemctl halt unmounts or remounts storage through systemd-shutdown before the CPUs stop, avoiding an abrupt reset of a busy rw Btrfs root. Expected kernel behavior: machine_halt stops CPUs with interrupts off and leaves power on.
With NOWAYOUT unset, a manager-side watchdog disarm can actually stop the timer. Apple's built-in driver is expected to implement stop, but that is not verified against the target source.

Upstream systemd applies RebootWatchdogUSec only to reboot/kexec and disarms on other shutdown verbs, so halt should not re-arm it. Setting it to 0 is still correct defense in depth (from memory of upstream source; target version not verified).
required_safeguards: Prove the disarm while Linux is still healthy, because CONFIG_WATCHDOG_SYSFS is unset and there is no state file. After RuntimeWatchdogUSec=0 and RebootWatchdogUSec=0 read back as 0 and /proc/1/fd shows no /dev/watchdog* (and no other process holds it), keep Linux up with SSH reachable for at least 45-60 s. Nothing pets the timer then, so surviving that window shows the 30 s hardware watchdog is stopped.
Never open /dev/watchdog* (wdctl or ioctl probes) to check state: opening can arm the timer and a close without magic close can leave it running.

Attribute the reset by onset time, not just eventual return: boot output on the M5 serial log (or the first SSH reachability) must start within a short window after the VDM (e.g. 15 s). If no onset follows the VDM promptly, classify VDM_NO_RESET even if the target returns later; a return near 120 s after halt could come from a still-armed 2 min reboot watchdog. A hold of at least 130 s instead of 40 s removes that ambiguity at only a time cost.
acceptance: Watchdog properties read back as 0, PID1 holds no watchdog fd, and the healthy-Linux no-pet window passes with no reset.
After systemctl halt: SSH down; serial shows the halt message if the kernel console is on serial, then silence through the hold window with no autonomous boot output.
macvdmtool reboot serial reaches the reboot VDM (rc and stdout recorded and classified per R4); boot onset follows promptly.

SSH returns with the pinned host key, a new boot_id, and the same kernel and /proc/cmdline as baseline; the current boot shows no Btrfs log replay or errors and no EFI dirty-bit warning; watchdog properties are back to 30 s / 2 min after boot.
Repeat at least 3 times before treating halted-CPU VDM recovery as qualified.
addendum_halt_based_external_reset.fallback_and_risk: A halted target has no SSH. If the VDM does not reset it (unproven: AppleHPM connected bit or SoC acceptance from a halted AP), recovery requires a physical power-button cycle, so the first runs need an operator. No poweroff: macvdmtool has no power-on.
addendum_halt_based_external_reset.what_it_does_not_qualify: Recovery from a panicked or crashed kernel, from an m1n1/HV/XNU park (m1n1 disables the watchdog and owns the USB-C proxy port; ACE/port interplay unknown), or from a target whose connected bit drops. Those remain S2 (optional panic) and S3.

non_goals: No DFU VDM, partitioning, boot-policy or firmware changes, persistent watchdog/panic configuration edits, power-off tests (macvdmtool has no power-on), or Maclab use. No large framework: one per-target lock, one serial reader, one macvdmtool invocation per reset, and SSH/boot_id checks suffice.
limits: No live observation by this reviewer; all target facts are relayed or inherited.
Whether the AppleHPM connected bit survives a hard hang, and whether the SoC accepts the reset VDM from a halted or panicked state, are unproven until S2.
Linux/systemd behavior is stated from general upstream semantics and must be verified on the target in each stage.
The kernel console may be on tty0 rather than serial; if so, attribution relies on M5 timestamps, boot_id and SSH timing.
